requirement: Each requirement and example definition badge MUST link to its evidence detail page, and each rendered requirement and example MUST be followed by a "See evidence" link to that page. Each detail page MUST link back to the definition's anchored badge and, when an index exists, to the index. Reference badges MUST continue to link to the definition. These links MUST resolve when a requirement name contains `.md`, as in `requirements.cli.mdbook`.
rationale:
**Verdict:** the sources satisfy `requirements.index.navigation`. I found no unmarked implementation and no unspecified behaviour in the marked code. I read the code and tests; I did not run the tests. **Obligations and where they are implemented** - **Definition badge links to the detail page.** `replace_definitions` (src/lib.rs:278) emits `` when a detail path exists in the `DetailPlan`. It falls back to a `span` only when there is no plan. - **"See evidence" link after each requirement and example.** The same function appends `

See evidence

`. Term definitions are skipped, which matches the requirement's wording ("requirement and example"). - **Detail page links back to the anchored badge and the index.** `render_detail_page` (src/index.rs:463) writes `[View definition](…#habeas-req-NAME)`. When an index exists, it also writes `[Requirements index](…)`. The anchor comes from `DefinitionKind::anchor` (src/lib.rs:82), which is marked `{impl}`. - **Index rows link to the detail pages.** `DetailPlan::populate` (src/index.rs:328) builds the rows, and its navigation block is marked `{impl}`. The `detail_path` and `is_detail_path` helpers are also marked `{impl}`. - **Reference badges still link to the definition.** `replace_references` (src/lib.rs:373) builds each reference link with `chapter_href` and the definition anchor. - **Links resolve for names containing `.md`.** `chapter_href` (src/lib.rs:464) rewrites `.md` to `%2Emd` in every generated href. Every href in these paths is built with it. **Tests** - `every_definition_gets_a_nested_detail_page_without_an_index` (src/lib.rs:845) uses a `cli.mdbook` name. It asserts the badge `href`, the "See evidence" link and the "View definition" link, including the `%2Emd` encoding. It also checks that no index link appears when there is no index, and that the "See evidence" count is exactly 3. - `index_shows_evidence_states_and_links_generated_chapters` (src/index.rs:1038) covers the case where an index exists. It checks the badge `href`, the index rows, the back link to the index, and the "View definition" link. - `links_preserve_requirement_names_containing_md` (src/lib.rs:951) unit-tests `chapter_href` in both directions, with and without an anchor. - `references_in_nested_chapters_link_to_the_requirement_definition` (src/lib.rs:1012) and the example-reference test check that reference badges still link to the definition. They are marked for `requirements.references.book_badges`, not for this requirement, but they still cover the obligation. **Minor observation:** no test puts a `.md` name in the index rows. Those rows use the same `chapter_href`, so the unit test covers them.
